/* .top-kv__left .-umamusume: 6.1333vw wide, 21.7 css of that on screen, and the
   reference string fills 168.9 css of length. In a vertical writing mode the
   *block* axis is horizontal, so the horizontal padding is the first value — it
   was the second, which left a negative content box and pushed the letters
   through both walls of the pill. Type is sized so the string lands on 149 css,
   the strings the official page runs are all caps, spaced wide, and the full
   phone capture (Screenshot_20261118-180923.jpg, DPR 3.5) puts the capsule at
   21.7 x 164.3 with glyphs only 7.7 css tall: Roboto Condensed 600 at 2.9vw
   (cap 7.5) with .5vw of tracking lands the ink on 158 and the capsule on 166. */

  /* Roboto, not Roboto Condensed: the site's plaque is a regular-width face —
     its capitals are as wide as they are tall (7.4 css each at a 7.43 pitch),
     which is why it fills 164 css with no tracking at all. */
  font-family: roboto, "Roboto Condensed", Arial, sans-serif;

     from the space at the ends of the capsule. In vertical writing mode the

/* ---------- In the Works (the site's News band) ----------
   The official band is a pink frame with a leaning ribbon straddling its top
   left corner, white cards inside it and a pink pill under them. All of it is
   CSS: the frame is a border on a rounded box, the ribbon is a skew, the card
   tags are clipped flags. Geometry from the reference capture (070505, 360 css
   wide): the frame runs x 15.8 -> 345.1 with a 3.1 css #FF79D0 edge round a
   #FFF0F7 panel; the cards run x 34.7 -> 326.2 (291.5 wide) with 9.4 css
   between them; the ribbon runs x 10 -> 137, y 134.6 -> 169, 13 degrees off
   square. The ground is the pale horseshoe art, and the key visual's photograph
   fades straight into it above the frame. */
.uma-news {
  background: #EFFEE7; border-top: 0; overflow: visible;
  padding: 9.5vw 4.4vw 9vw;
  /* the band climbs into the key visual's fade, so the pale ground and the ribbon sit at the
     level where the picture was already dissolving, not 45 css below it */
  margin-top: -6vw;
}
/* The ground is a plain <img>, the way every other band in this profile carries its
   artwork. A CSS background-image here never reached the live page: the band came out as
   flat #EFFEE7 with the pattern missing, while the card art from the same commit loaded,
   so the url() is the only thing that could have failed. The image is 1000 x 1833, so at
   any width it is 1.833 x the width tall; where a band grows past that, the #EFFEE7 under
   it finishes the job. */
.uma-news-ground {
  position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 100%;

}

/* ---------- About (sky) ---------- */
.uma-about {
  background: #4BA8F5;
  /* The band is now exactly as tall as the official stylesheet makes it. From
     _app/immutable/assets/2.BtMVfDfi.css:
       .top-about.svelte-jhqwtp{height:122.6666666667vw}                 (<=899.98)
       @media (min-width:900px){.top-about{height:62.5vw}}
       @media (min-width:2000px){.top-about{height:1250px}}
     122.6667vw is 460px in the site's 375px design. A fixed height, because the card no
     longer sits in the flow (it stands in for .about-movie-thumb, which is absolutely
     centred), so nothing below it is sizing the band any more. border-box keeps the 26px
     top padding inside that height, which is what puts top:50% on the band's real middle. */
  box-sizing: border-box;
  height: 122.6667vw;
  padding-bottom: 0;
}
/* The site's white title plate sits 31 css under the band's top edge (860 device on the
   132227 capture, band top 760); the shared 26px section padding leaves ours 5 short, and
   this is the one band where the gap was measured against the real thing. */
.uma-about .uma-tag-wrap { margin-top: 5px; }
/* The three cut-outs, in the card's own free upper-right corner (fig-jet / fig-car /
   fig-horse, built by tools/make-figs.py). The card's body is a column of short lines — the
   role plate, the name, the follower count — and none of them reaches the right edge, so the
   corner above the break is empty white at every width: 125 x 74 css at 390, 246 x 145 at
   1280. The row is pinned to that corner by the body's own padding (4vw / 3.8vw, the numbers
   --uma-k already scales), and it is sized by --uma-k too, so it stays the same small thing
   against the copy instead of becoming furniture on a desktop. One height for all three, so
   they sit on the break like a row of stickers. */
.uma-about-figs {
  position: absolute !important; z-index: 3;
  top: 4vw !important; right: 3.8vw !important;
  display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: .5vw;
  pointer-events: none;
}
/* Everything here is plain vw and !important on purpose. Two things go wrong on the live
   page that a local render never shows: Janitor's own reset puts `height: auto !important`
   on images, and their pipeline does not always keep the `:root` rule that defines
   --uma-k, which turns every calc() that reads it into an invalid declaration. A missing
   --uma-k is survivable (`--uma-k, 1` everywhere), a missing height is not: three 320px
   renders loose in a 364px card, wide enough to widen the document and drag the centred
   card off screen. So the size is written out at each breakpoint instead of derived. */
.uma-about-ph .uma-about-figs img {
  display: block !important;
  width: auto !important; max-width: none !important;
  height: 5.75vw !important;
  filter: drop-shadow(0 .22vw .7vw rgba(12,54,96,.30));
}
@media (min-width: 900px) {
  .uma-about-figs { top: 2.38vw !important; right: 2.26vw !important; gap: .3vw; }
  .uma-about-ph .uma-about-figs img { height: 3.42vw !important; }
}
@media (min-width: 2000px) {

/* Our copy of the About art is the landscape crop, 1100 x 688, while the official phone page
   runs a taller crop of the same painting, so the stands sit lower there. Covering a 360 x 446
   band with this one means showing about half of its width: the left half keeps the roofline
   low and the sky open, which is the reference's read, where centring it raised the stands
   across the whole right side. */
.uma-about .uma-sec-bg { object-position: 20% 50%; opacity: 1; }
/* The pink corner. On the reference the About art runs out under a pink diagonal with white
   showing past its lower edge, and that band is part of their taller crop: our window only
   reaches the middle of the wide painting, so the corner is drawn here instead, to the same
   geometry. Off the capture, at 3.5 px per css: the edge falls 0.42 css per css across the
   width, the band is 62 css deep, and its upper edge meets the right edge 112 css above the
   section's bottom. In vw that is 42.2, 17.2 and 31.1, on a 60vw tall plate at the bottom. */
.uma-about::before,
.uma-about::after {
  content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0;
  height: 60vw; z-index: 1; pointer-events: none;
}
.uma-about::before {
  background: #FF6DC8;
  clip-path: polygon(0 69.8vw, 100% 27.5vw, 100% 44vw, 0 86.3vw);
}
.uma-about::after {
  background: #fff;
  clip-path: polygon(0 86.3vw, 100% 44vw, 100% 60vw, 0 60vw);
}
/* The band's texture, the UMA emblem and URA lettering, is a PNG sized to the same 5:3 box as
   the layers above and drawn on the same seat as the polygon, so the two coincide at every
   width: the band is textured edge to edge and the flat pink underneath is only the fallback
   for a slow image. tools/make-about-pink.py builds it. */
.uma-about-pink {
  position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0;
  width: 100%; height: 60vw; z-index: 1; pointer-events: none;
  /* the same parallelogram as the band itself, so the texture's edge is the band's edge and
     not the image's own antialiased one: no pale line where the sheet stops */
  clip-path: polygon(0 69.8vw, 100% 27.5vw, 100% 44vw, 0 86.3vw);
}
/* The profile card. It stands in for the site's About video block, so it takes that
   block's numbers straight from 2.BtMVfDfi.css:

     .top-about .about-movie-thumb{overflow:hidden;position:absolute;z-index:1;
        top:50%;left:50%;transform:translate3d(-50%,-50%,0);
        filter:drop-shadow(.4vw .4vw 1.3333333333vw rgba(0,0,0,.25))}
     @media (max-width:899.98px){.about-movie-thumb{width:93.3333333333vw;height:50.1333333333vw}}
     @media (min-width:900px){.about-movie-thumb{width:55.5555555556vw;height:31.25vw}}
     @media (min-width:2000px){.about-movie-thumb{width:1111.1111px;height:625px}}

   93.3333 x 50.1333vw is 350 x 188 in the 375px design: inset 3.3333vw from either edge of
   the band, 1.862:1, and centred on it — not the full-bleed 2.6:1 ribbon of the last pass.
   The soft shadow is theirs too; the corner stays square, which the stylesheet confirms
   (no radius on the block). */
/* One number sizes everything inside the card. The block is 93.3333vw wide on a phone and
   55.5556vw on a desktop, so the same design has to be drawn 0.595x smaller there to keep its
   proportions: --uma-k is that ratio, and every inner size is written as calc(<mobile vw> * k).
   It lives on :root because the live follower count, which is not a child of the card, has to
   read the same number. */
:root { --uma-k: 1; }
@media (min-width: 900px) { :root { --uma-k: .5955; } }

.uma-about-ph {
  position: absolute; z-index: 2;
  left: 50%; top: 50%;
  width: 93.3333vw; height: 50.1333vw;
  transform: translate3d(-50%, -50%, 0);
  filter: drop-shadow(.4vw .4vw 1.3333vw rgba(0,0,0,.25));
  background: #fff;
  border-radius: 0; box-shadow: none;
  box-sizing: border-box; display: flex; overflow: hidden;
  font-family: "Roboto Condensed", roboto, Arial, sans-serif;
}

}

  flex: 1; min-width: 0; padding: calc(4vw * var(--uma-k, 1)) calc(3.8vw * var(--uma-k, 1));
  /* border-box, or the padding is added to the height the card gives this column and the last
     line of the bio is pushed past the card's edge. With it, the column's content is exactly
     the card's inside: 4vw of air at the top of the chip and at the foot of the bio. */
  box-sizing: border-box;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: center;
}
.uma-tc-role {

  /* upright, widely tracked caps: the display face is already carrying the italics, so the
     chip's job is to be quiet and unmistakably a label. Roboto at 700 keeps the small size
     legible where the condensed face would close its counters up. */
  font-family: roboto, "Roboto", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: calc(2vw * var(--uma-k, 1)); font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .01em; text-transform: none;
  padding: calc(.95vw * var(--uma-k, 1)) calc(2.1vw * var(--uma-k, 1)) calc(.85vw * var(--uma-k, 1));

}

  color: #13294B; letter-spacing: -.015em; margin: calc(1.4vw * var(--uma-k, 1)) 0 0;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
.uma-tc-fol {
  /* Label first, number second, both on one baseline. The order matters: the live count
     replaces the stand-in's digits and is usually shorter, so anything to the number's left
     would move when it changes. Here the label is pinned to the card's margin and the number
     grows into empty card instead, which keeps the gap identical for "1" and "128,043". */
  display: flex; align-items: baseline;
  gap: calc(1.6vw * var(--uma-k, 1));
  margin-top: calc(1.2vw * var(--uma-k, 1));

/* ---------- the break ----------
   His own divider: the site's horseshoe sitting in a rule that runs the column's width. It is
   an <img> and not a mask or a background — this profile drops every url() the stylesheet
   carries, so the file itself is cut out and coloured the brand pink, and CSS only places it. */
.uma-tc-break {
  display: block; width: 100%; height: auto;
  margin: calc(2.2vw * var(--uma-k, 1)) 0 calc(2vw * var(--uma-k, 1));
}
.uma-tc-bio {
  /* A scroll box, not a paragraph. The card is a fixed 50.1333vw tall whatever is in it, so
     the bio takes what the name, chip, count and rule leave over — and when the text is
     longer than that, it scrolls here instead of pushing the card or the page. The cap keeps
     the block's old centred seat: at any width the box tops out at the height that leaves the
     surrounding columns balanced, and justify-content: center spends whatever is left above
     and below it. min-height: 0 is what lets it shrink on a short card rather than overflow. */
  flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0;
  overflow-y: auto; overscroll-behavior: contain; -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;
  /* a thin bar in the card's own colours: pink thumb, faint track, no arrows */
  scrollbar-width: thin;
  scrollbar-color: #F0A6CE rgba(19,41,75,.07);
  /* the last line fades rather than being sliced by the box's edge: the same read the band
     wanted, and it is what tells a thumb that there is more under it */
  -webkit-mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, #000 0 74%, rgba(0,0,0,.12) 100%);
  mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, #000 0 74%, rgba(0,0,0,.12) 100%);
  padding-right: calc(.7vw * var(--uma-k, 1));
  font-family: roboto, "Roboto", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: calc(2.95vw * var(--uma-k, 1)); line-height: 1.52; color: #3E5A76;
  font-weight: 400; margin: 0; text-wrap: pretty;
}
.uma-tc-bio::-webkit-scrollbar { width: calc(.85vw * var(--uma-k, 1)); }
.uma-tc-bio::-webkit-scrollbar-track { background: rgba(19,41,75,.07); border-radius: 99px; }
.uma-tc-bio::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: #F0A6CE; border-radius: 99px; }
.uma-tc-bio::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover { background: #E5348A; }
/* a full line of air between paragraphs, so each one reads as its own thought instead of
   running on from the last — the block is scrolled, not skimmed, and this is the only
   structure it gets */
.uma-tc-bio p { margin: 0 0 calc(1.5vw * var(--uma-k, 1)); }
.uma-tc-bio p:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }
/* The greeting is the block's one bit of hierarchy: a shade larger and in the card's navy
   rather than the body blue, so the eye lands on it first. Everything under it stays one
   size — his copy is a run of facts, and the air between paragraphs is what separates them. */
.uma-tc-bio p:first-child { font-size: calc(3.15vw * var(--uma-k, 1)); line-height: 1.42; color: #13294B; }
/* Bold is for the handful of facts worth a thumb: the names he goes by, what he is, the number
   the whole paragraph hangs on, the one race he names. Navy rather than body blue, so a bold
   word reads as a headword and not as a link. */
.uma-tc-bio strong { font-weight: 700; color: #13294B; }
/* the same break, quieter and inside the scroll: a page break between movements, not a rule */
.uma-tc-bio .uma-tc-break {
  margin: calc(2.6vw * var(--uma-k, 1)) 0 calc(2.4vw * var(--uma-k, 1));
  opacity: .45;
}

/* ---------- the site's own header bar (markup, not CSS art) ---------- */
/* No second header. The wordmark is pinned over Janitor's own profile bar and
   Janitor's title is made transparent behind it, so the site mark sits inside
   the real header instead of a copy of it. */
/* The wordmark rides inside Janitor's own bar. This row takes no height of its
   own: it is lifted straight onto their 44px bar and never paints a band, so
   there is no second header to see. Their bar keeps its blue from the page
   background (its own paint is cleared below), which also means the wordmark
   shows through even when their bar wins the stacking order. */
/* Anchored to the FOOT of Janitor's bar rather than its top, so the wordmark
   lands inside the bar whatever height their bar happens to be: the row is
   pulled up by its own height and gives that height straight back to the flow. */
/* Their bar cannot hold an <img> (this profile strips every CSS image
   reference, and the markup of that bar is not ours to edit). So the site's
   wordmark and horseshoe are drawn as a fixed layer at the top of the viewport
   with the largest z-index there is: their own bar stays exactly as Janitor
   paints it underneath, buttons and caption included, and the two marks sit on
   it. Height follows a 44-52px bar, which is what the live site uses. */
.uma-hdr {
  position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; z-index: 2147483647;
  height: 57px; margin: 0;
  display: flex; align-items: flex-start; justify-content: space-between;
  padding: 0; background: #0F57FB; pointer-events: none;
}
.uma-hdr-brand { display: block; line-height: 0; }
/* narrow phones: the label must not creep into the first plate, nor the
   accounts row crowd itself */

  .uma-playnow { padding-right: 5px; }

/* .header__wrapper .-logo: width 32.5333vw, margin-left 4vw */
/* .header__wrapper .-logo.is-top.is-large on the site: the mark starts larger
   than the bar and settles down to its normal width once the page moves. */
/* .header__wrapper .-logo, measured off two screenshots of the official page
   (1260 px wide, 360 CSS px, DPR 3.5):
     settled   box 117.0 x 34.6 css at x 14.9, y 103.5  -> 32.51vw
     at rest   box 199.9 x 59.0 css at x 15.7, y 104.0  -> 55.53vw
   So: left 4vw, top 10px, and only the width changes as the page moves. The
   mark is anchored near the top rather than centred, which is why the larger
   one hangs out of the 57px bar and the small one does not. */
.uma-hdr-brand img {
  display: block; width: 32.5333vw; height: auto;
  margin-left: 4vw; margin-top: 10px;
}
/* A scroll timeline cannot attach to this layer: the band is position:fixed and
   Chrome resolves a fixed subtree against the viewport, so scroll() has nothing
   to follow (verified in a harness built on Janitor's own stylesheet and
   markup). A *view* timeline is a different animal — it tracks the box of an
   element that really is in the flow — so a zero-height sentinel parked one
   screen down -- less the height of Janitor's own bar, which is what the shell
   starts under -- gives us "0 at the top of the page, 1 after V px of scroll". timeline-scope hoists that name up to the shell so the fixed
   wordmark can reference it. */
.uma-shell { timeline-scope: --uma-settle; }
.uma-sentinel {
  position: absolute; left: 0; top: calc(100vh - 64px); width: 0; height: 0;
  view-timeline: --uma-settle block; pointer-events: none;
}
@supports (animation-timeline: --uma-settle) {
  @keyframes uma-logo-settle {
    from { width: 55.5333vw; }
    to   { width: 32.5333vw; }
  }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
    .uma-hdr-brand img {
      animation: uma-logo-settle linear both;
      animation-timeline: --uma-settle;
      animation-range: cover 0% cover 14%;
    }
  }
}

   same band at its bottom (padding-bottom below) so no row can end up behind

/* The list above names the classes the profile card had when it was measured. Janitor renames
   them freely, and a renamed row does not disappear: it stays as an empty, transparent band the
   height of the avatar and the handle, which shows the page behind it as a stretch of colour
   under the bar — a header that looks like it grew overnight. So the rule now says what to keep
   instead of what to drop: inside the profile card, the About block is the only survivor, and
   anything that merely *contains* it is left alone (:has keeps the wrapper, and a browser
   without :has simply drops this rule and falls back to the list above). */
.pp-uc-background > *:not(.pp-uc-about-me):not(.profile-about-me):not(:has(.pp-uc-about-me)):not(:has(.profile-about-me)) {
  display: none !important;
}

   the wordmark and the menu dial in half. Only one header can own the top of
   the page: ours does, Janitor's keeps its place at the top of the document. */

/* Sections settle in as they arrive, so the page has some life as you scroll.
   Scroll-driven only, and only when the reader has not asked for less motion. */

    from { opacity: .35; transform: translateY(26px); }
    to   { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
  }

    .uma-sec > .uma-tag-wrap,
    .uma-sec > .uma-hl,
    .uma-sec > .uma-card,
    .uma-sec > .uma-more,

/* The two wider-step sizes are the site's own: the same block is 55.5556 x 31.25vw from 900
   (400 x 225 in their 720px desktop design, i.e. 16:9) and a flat 1111.1 x 625px past 2000.
   Everything inside the card is sized in vw, so it grows with the card and needs no other
   breakpoint except the last one, where the card stops growing in px terms. */
@media (min-width: 900px) {
  .uma-about { height: 62.5vw; }
  .uma-play { height: 62.5vw; }
  .uma-about-ph { width: 55.5556vw; height: 31.25vw; }
}

  .uma-about { height: 1250px; }
  .uma-play { height: 1250px; }
  .uma-about-ph { width: 1111.1111px; height: 625px; }
  /* the card is a flat size from here, so the corner row is too (0.5955 * 1vw at 2000) */
  /* the card is a flat size from here, so the type stops being fluid: 1vw is 20px at 2000,
     and 0.5955 * 20 turns the mobile vw values above into their pixel equivalents */
  .uma-tc-body { padding: 47.6px 45.3px; }
  .uma-tc-role { font-size: 23.8px; padding: 11.3px 25px 10.1px; }
  .uma-tc-name { font-size: 70.3px; margin-top: 16.7px; }
  .uma-tc-fol { margin-top: 14.3px; gap: 19px; }
  .uma-tc-fol span { font-size: 22.6px; }
  .uma-tc-fol b { font-size: 56px; }
  .uma-tc-break { margin: 26px 0 23.8px; }
  .uma-tc-bio .uma-tc-break { margin: 30.9px 0 28.5px; }
  .uma-tc-bio { font-size: 35.1px; padding-right: 8.3px; }
  .uma-tc-bio p:first-child { font-size: 37.5px; }
  .uma-tc-bio::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 10.1px; }
}
/* Live binding. The profile's own avatar and follower count are lifted into the card: they
   already exist in the page (Janitor renders them in .pp-uc-background, which this theme hides),
   and anchor positioning places an element against a named element inside the same containing
   block, so the real .pp-uc-avatar-container can sit exactly on .uma-tc-port without being a DOM
   child of it.

   Every geometric value is written twice: first parked off-canvas at zero size, then the
   anchor()/anchor-size() value that replaces it. A browser that parses the @supports test but
   cannot resolve the anchor therefore keeps the parked values and paints nothing, instead of
   dropping a full-size avatar at the top of the page. The stand-in portrait and number are never
   hidden, so a failed binding still shows a finished card; when the binding works the live
   follower count covers the stand-in exactly (same box, opaque card colour). */
.uma-tc-port { anchor-name: --uma-pfp; }
.uma-tc-fol b { display: inline-block; anchor-name: --uma-fol; }
@supports (position-anchor: --uma-pfp) {
  /* Deliberately NOT position:relative here. An anchor only counts while it shares a
     containing block with the element being placed, and Janitor is free to move the About Me
     block out of .pp-uc-background between releases (its own Studio mock and the September
     capture already disagree about nothing else). Leaving the wrapper static pushes the
     containing block up to whatever ancestor holds both, which is true for either layout —
     verified against the captured page with the block inside the wrapper and outside it. */
  .pp-uc-background { position: static !important; }
  .pp-uc-background .profile-info-wrapper-box,
  .pp-uc-background .profile-info-stack {
    position: static !important; overflow: visible !important;
  }
  /* the rows still have to be rendered for their children to be, so they are kept and
     flattened to nothing */
  .pp-uc-background .profile-info-hstack,
  .pp-uc-background .profile-info-stack-inner {
    display: block !important; position: static !important;
    height: 0 !important; min-height: 0 !important;
    margin: 0 !important; padding: 0 !important; overflow: visible !important;
  }
  .pp-uc-background .profile-info-stack-inner > *:not(.pp-uc-followers-count) {
    display: none !important;
  }
  .pp-uc-background .pp-uc-avatar-container {
    display: block !important; position: absolute !important;
    top: -9999px !important; left: -9999px !important;
    width: 0 !important; height: 0 !important; overflow: hidden !important;
    top: anchor(--uma-pfp top, -9999px) !important;
    left: anchor(--uma-pfp left, -9999px) !important;
    width: anchor-size(--uma-pfp width, 0px) !important;
    height: anchor-size(--uma-pfp height, 0px) !important;
    margin: 0 !important; padding: 0 !important; border: 0 !important;
    border-radius: 0 !important; background: none !important; box-shadow: none !important;
    z-index: 4;
  }
  .pp-uc-background .pp-uc-avatar-container > a { display: none !important; }
  .pp-uc-background .pp-uc-avatar,
  .pp-uc-background .pp-uc-avatar-container img {
    display: block !important; width: 100% !important; height: 100% !important;
    object-fit: cover !important; border-radius: 0 !important;
  }
  .pp-uc-background .pp-uc-followers-count {
    display: block !important; position: absolute !important;
    top: -9999px !important; left: -9999px !important;
    width: 0 !important; height: 0 !important; overflow: hidden !important;
    top: anchor(--uma-fol top, -9999px) !important;
    left: anchor(--uma-fol left, -9999px) !important;
    /* a touch wider than the stand-in box: the italic glyphs overhang their advance width,
       and a sliver of the old number would otherwise peek out beside the live one */
    width: calc(anchor-size(--uma-fol width, 0px) + 1.4vw) !important;
    height: calc(anchor-size(--uma-fol height, 0px) + 1vw) !important;
    overflow: visible !important;
    margin: 0 !important; padding: 0 !important; white-space: nowrap !important;
    background: #fff !important;
    font-family: "Roboto Condensed", roboto, Arial, sans-serif !important;
    font-style: italic; font-weight: 900 !important;
    font-size: calc(4.7vw * var(--uma-k, 1)) !important;
    line-height: 1.05 !important; color: #E5348A !important;
    z-index: 5;
  }
  .pp-uc-background .pp-uc-followers-count span + span { display: none !important; }
  /* the card stops growing with the viewport at 2000 (it is a flat 1111px there), so the live
     number has to leave vw at the same point as the stand-in it covers */
  @media (min-width: 2000px) {
    .pp-uc-background .pp-uc-followers-count { font-size: 56px !important; }
  }
}
</style>

      <details class="uma-card">
        <summary>
          <span class="uma-meta"><span class="uma-pill">Production</span><span class="uma-date">2026/10/30 11:12 (UTC)</span></span>
          <span class="uma-card-txt">The shift from quality over quantity.</span>
          <span class="uma-card-go">&#187;&#187;</span>
        </summary>
        <div class="uma-cbody">
          <p>I am moving away from <i>only</i> making Umamusume bots. I want to branch out into new fandoms, try fresh ideas, and introduce my work to different communities. With that, the January 2027 Lorebooks release target is being pushed back to <b>February or March 2027</b>. Looking at the math, finishing by January meant updating each lorebook in just a week and a half. I have put way too much effort into these lorebooks to rush them now, so taking a bit more time is definitely the right move.</p>
        </div>
      </details>

      <details class="uma-card">
        <summary>
          <span class="uma-meta"><span class="uma-pill">Schedule</span><span class="uma-date">2026/11/07 01:34 (UTC)</span></span>
          <span class="uma-card-txt">What @uma_enjoyer's schedule in bot creation looks like.</span>
          <span class="uma-card-go">&#187;&#187;</span>
        </summary>
        <div class="uma-cbody">
          <p>My character cards will usually be released on weekends. During the week I am usually off thinking up scenarios and experimenting with lorebook prototypes that may be used for the next update of my passion project. Expect probably like 2 to 4 bots a week. It would commonly be 2, that is what I have to trade in order to get higher quality creations. 4 is when I have excess free time. Pick your time zone below and it opens with my schedules.</p>
          <div class="uma-tzlist">
        <details class="uma-tz">
          <summary>UTC-08 &middot; LOS ANGELES (WINTER)</summary>

  <!-- ── About ─────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
  <div class="uma-sec uma-about" id="about">
    <img class="uma-sec-bg" alt="" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lanzopanzo2013-eng/puppeteer@fa8143d4090cc4fd61e9796724e261aefa5ee977/uma-profile/assets/site/about_bg.jpg">
    <img class="uma-about-pink" alt="" aria-hidden="true" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lanzopanzo2013-eng/puppeteer@dca1b39a0cc10301c6f20532399e4a22bc97a2f0/uma-profile/assets/site/about-pink-full.png">
    <div class="uma-tag-wrap"><div class="uma-tag blue uma-tag-white"><span>About Me</span></div></div>

    <div class="uma-about-ph">
      <div class="uma-tc-port">
        <img class="uma-tc-pfp" alt="" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lanzopanzo2013-eng/puppeteer@9c867618abe4b16f7a7a976fb589e7aceedcea73/uma-profile/assets/site/pfp.jpg">
      </div>
      <div class="uma-tc-body">
        <span class="uma-tc-role"><i>@uma_enjoyer</i></span>
        <div class="uma-tc-name">Fuji/Aki</div>
        <div class="uma-tc-fol"><span>Followers</span><b>128,043</b></div>
        <img class="uma-tc-break" alt="" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lanzopanzo2013-eng/puppeteer@071c6ccac752ace2c0d8a19a4b5ecfa6d3cffdd8/uma-profile/assets/site/horseshoe-break.png">
        <div class="uma-tc-bio">
          <p>Hi reader, I am uma_enjoyer, and you can call me <strong>Fuji or Aki</strong>. I started creating bots back in 2023, focusing on realistic Japanese life scenarios all the way to <strong>Initial D</strong>, then in spring I stopped and switched to Janitor AI, and by August 2026 I was making story-first Umamusume bots.</p>
          <p>As a person I am male, he/him, <strong>half Filipino and half Japanese</strong>, and I speak three languages. They are English, Tagalog and Japanese, though my vocabulary is just okay in all of them. I do motorsports in real life and on the simulator, and I am a professional in the sport. I am a young adult who still does college classes, I am single, and I take life seriously to the fullest.</p>
          <img class="uma-tc-break" alt="" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lanzopanzo2013-eng/puppeteer@071c6ccac752ace2c0d8a19a4b5ecfa6d3cffdd8/uma-profile/assets/site/horseshoe-break.png">
          <p>I love cars a lot, like, really. Almost <strong>70%</strong> of the fun in my whole life comes from the car life, and that is thanks to my dad. When I was an elementary/middle schooler he was a well-known member of a car club and always took me around car meets and track days. It is unfortunate that he passed away, just recently, but for my family's privacy I won't go deeper than that. I compete in a lot of motorsport competitions, and no, I am not a rich kid who wants to race. <strong>The wins pay for my entrance fees.</strong></p>
          <p>AI is another thing I find highly interesting. I love experimenting with LLMs, I would consider myself a great prompter, and I could see myself having a job related to AI someday too. I love cats, and dogs too, and I don't hate any kind of housepet at all. I used to play <strong>War Thunder and Call of Duty</strong> all the time during COVID, so I know a lot when it comes to military vehicles, which is one of my strengths in bot creation. I love the world of desktops too, so if you want to discuss PC parts, I can happily take part.</p>
          <p>I believe in God, but I will not specify which God because of privacy reasons, and on that note I keep my identity private so I don't get known for this in real life. In bot creation I specialize in <strong>lorebooks, RPG and Japan life scenarios</strong>. I can create any kind of bot, although I am weak when it comes to smut and I don't have much experience with it, so if you are a smut-focused person, I am not for you to like.</p>
          <img class="uma-tc-break" alt="" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lanzopanzo2013-eng/puppeteer@071c6ccac752ace2c0d8a19a4b5ecfa6d3cffdd8/uma-profile/assets/site/horseshoe-break.png">
          <p>Oh, and I do love horse racing too. One of my notable events was spectating from the grandstands at the <strong>Arima Kinen, 2022</strong>. I got myself a QR ticket and I watched <strong>Equinox</strong> win. To be fair I am not that passionate about it compared to cars, but I still have some passion for horse racing.</p>
          <p>And then there is Umamusume. I first watched season 1 because my friends invited me to watch with them, then I played <strong>Umamusume Pretty Derby</strong> by March 2021. I was not a try-hard at the game, I only played it lightly until now to be honest, and I think that is going to be the same forever, although I did watch all the anime series Umamusume has to offer, which strengthened my passion for these horsegirls.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!-- the three cut-outs, in the card's own empty corner -->
      <div class="uma-about-figs" aria-hidden="true">
        <img class="fig-jet" alt="" width="34" height="22" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lanzopanzo2013-eng/puppeteer@003d995/uma-profile/assets/site/fig-jet.png">
        <img class="fig-car" alt="" width="51" height="22" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lanzopanzo2013-eng/puppeteer@003d995/uma-profile/assets/site/fig-car.png">

      </div>
    </div>
